p: PyTorch Essentials
x: PyTorch is an open-source Python library for deep learning, originally released by Meta AI in 2016 and now governed by the PyTorch Foundation. It has been the most widely used framework in machine-learning research for years, and it is the substrate of nearly every open LLM codebase, from Hugging Face Transformers to vLLM, SGLang, Megatron-LM and veRL. Its popularity comes from a design that feels like ordinary Python: you write imperative code, run it line by line, inspect any value, and get gradients for free.

An automatic differentiation engine ( autograd ): it records the operations applied to tensors and computes gradients by traversing that record backwards. A deep-learning library : modules (layers), loss functions, optimisers, data loading and distributed training utilities built on top of the first two. Figure 2.2: The PyTorch stack

p: PyTorch Essentials
x: PyTorch infers the data type ( dtype ) from the input: Python integers become torch.int64 , Python floats become torch.float32 . Token ids are integers ( int64 by default, since embedding lookups expect it); everything that is learned or computed is floating point. Converting is explicit: x.to(torch.bfloat16) or x.float() . The default float32 is a sensible balance of precision and cost on CPUs, but on modern accelerators most LLM arithmetic runs in 16-bit or even 8-bit formats, which we examine in Section  2.2.4 .

x: The simplest way to use several GPUs is data parallelism with PyTorch’s DistributedDataParallel (DDP). One process is launched per GPU; each holds a full replica of the model and receives a different slice of every global batch. After the backward pass, gradients are averaged across processes with an all-reduce collective, so every replica applies the same update and the replicas stay identical (Figure  2.7 ).
